chunks: From him, from Sa'id ibn Abdillah, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar, from Ja'far (AS), from his father (AS):

That Ali (peace be upon him) did not perform the ritual washing (ghusl) for Ammar ibn Yasir, nor for Hashim ibn Utba al-Mirqal, buried them both in their garments, and did not perform the funeral prayer over them.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The narrator's statement 'and did not perform the prayer over them' is an error (wahm) on the part of the narrator, because the funeral prayer does not lapse for the deceased under any circumstance whatsoever — as is indicated by [what follows].

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the funeral prayer (salat al-mayyit), which is a communal obligation (fard kifaya)
key_terms.وَهْمٌ: transmitter's error — an inadvertent mistake in narration
key_terms.يُغَسِّلْ: performs the ritual washing of the deceased (ghusl al-mayyit)

ai.seo_question: In Shia jurisprudence, is the ghusl and funeral prayer waived for martyrs killed in battle?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam Ali (AS) did not perform the ritual washing (ghusl) for Ammar ibn Yasir and Hashim ibn Utba al-Mirqal — both martyred at the Battle of Siffin — and buried them in their garments. Sheikh Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi then corrects the narrator's additional claim that the funeral prayer was also omitted, clarifying that the funeral prayer (salat al-mayyit) is never waived for the deceased under any circumstance in Shia jurisprudence, and that this part of the narration constitutes a transmitter's error (wahm).
